traceability.notes:
The specification docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md describes clear, specific, and consistent error messages across all core traceability rules, plus appropriate severity levels.
Concrete implementation evidence: - Each listed rule (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) defines explicit meta.messages templates using ESLint best practices and shared conventions (functionName, details, path/storyPath/reqId). - Error-reporting helpers (coreReportMissing, annotation-checker, valid-annotation-format validators, valid-story-reference helpers, valid-req-reference helpers) wire these message templates into context.report with precise node locations and rich data payloads. - Auto-fixes and suggestions are provided where appropriate: require-story-annotation uses ESLint suggestions with descriptive text; branch and format rules offer safe fixers that insert or normalize annotations while tests assert expected fixed code. - Error handling is defensive: helpers catch internal errors and either swallow them (with optional debug logging) or convert filesystem/configuration failures into explicit diagnostics (fileAccessError, invalidRuleConfiguration), verified by dedicated tests. - Plugin-level configs (recommended and strict) centralize severity mapping so missing annotations/references are errors and format issues are warnings, with tests confirming this behavior.
All Story 007.0 acceptance criteria and named requirements (REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, LOCATION, SUGGESTION, CONTEXT, CONSISTENCY, SEVERITY, HANDLING) are covered by targeted, passing tests that explicitly reference this story file. Based on this concrete code and test evidence, the story is fully implemented and verified.
